players.product: Power Systems division: backup engines and gas engines for prime power at data centres; next-generation engine to replace the Series 4000, targeting the data centre market with increased power density (launch 2028)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Tufan Erginbilgic on Power Systems and hyperscalers: 'we do more content for hyperscalers than any other customer in data center space' - not only standalone engines but gensets and enclosures (containers), all carrying margin; Rolls-Royce manages hyperscalers globally with a global account because its dealer / distributor contracts do not stop it (for other data centres the distributors do the enclosures). He wants strategic partnerships with some hyperscalers - they help implement Rolls-Royce's digitization agenda while it helps them with data centres and maintenance, plus long-term service agreements modelled on Civil Aerospace - discussed at CEO level. Power Systems services growth was double digit in the last two years including this year; with it he plans to variabilize some costs and move more of the supply chain to low-cost countries.

CEO Tufan Erginbilgic on Defence: the big growth will start 2028 onwards - MV75 is 'a huge program', OE as well as aftermarket, with B-52 re-engining following pretty closely, while GCAP and AUKUS are scaling up in the U.K.; legacy programmes are getting more orders than expected because of world events - Eurofighter order-book visibility now runs to the 2030s and more A330 MRTT+ orders are coming. On the H1 Defence margin of 21%: not sustainable because the aftermarket / OE mix favoured aftermarket, but the self-help improvement will stay - 'our margins will be higher than before, but lower than 21%.'
quarterly_data.figure: Defence margins higher than before but lower than 21%; major programme production from 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Tufan Erginbilgic: Rolls-Royce is now market leader in gas turbine-based autonomous systems (not the low-end electricity / diesel-based segment, where 'there is no margin to capture'). MQ-25 (large autonomous) was given to Rolls-Royce, successfully flight tested and will start production; Germany and the U.K. came with CCA contracts for medium gas turbine-based systems, all fully funded programmes; at the smaller end it has agreed a joint venture partnership with a company it did not name. With the U.S., Germany and the U.K. committed to development across the full range, he expects first funded programmes and then a move to production.

CEO Tufan Erginbilgic on Civil pricing: Rolls-Royce signs LTSA contracts every day; since the 2023 deal framework it has increased pricing because significant product cost inflation remains - elemental costs went up significantly on export controls from some countries and their use in missile production, and rare earth prices rose after one country's export controls; the company is taking actions so these costs do not dilute its business model. On GE Aerospace's proposed acquisition of Consolidated Precision Products: Rolls-Royce already makes turbines and blades in-house; its Civil Aerospace business does not do much with CPP while its Defence business has some work with it; he expects the deal to change the dynamics in casting and forging, a part of the value chain that 'needs to add capacity'. Next-generation narrowbody: very close product dialogue with Boeing and Airbus, but no commercial conversation at this point.
